name: addpipe24_han_carlson
rationale: Prior full Kogge-Stone matched baseline WNS but at +19 area (O(n log n) combine nodes); Sklansky cut area but lost WNS due to high-fanout combine nodes; both flat-SOP and KS-tree block-CLA(4) landed in between without beating baseline reward. A Han-Carlson adder is a well-known sparse hybrid: it first pairwise-combines all 24 bits into 12 group G/P terms (1 level), builds a full Kogge-Stone prefix tree only over that half-size (12-element) reduced array (uniform 2-input combine nodes, low fanout, 4 levels), then does one cheap fix-up level to resolve the remaining half of the carries. This gives roughly half the combine-node count of full 24-bit Kogge-Stone (since the expensive O(n log n) tree only spans n/2 elements) while adding only one extra logic level versus full KS/Sklansky (6 vs 5), which should land at markedly lower area than both KS (549.8) and CLA-block4 variants, at a WNS cost expected to be smaller than Sklansky's (since combine fan-in/fan-out stays uniformly small, unlike Sklansky's later-level wide-fanout reference nodes). This targets a new non-dominated area/WNS point between Sklansky (474.8/7.435) and the tool-inferred baseline (530.9/7.519).
